name: Xmind
tagline: Desktop and mobile mind maps, outlines, and presentation modes

pricing.basis: paid plan; billing basis requires review
pricing.native: Public paid plan exists; amount not safely recovered
pricing.notes: The official pricing URL is recorded, but a stable current amount was not safely recoverable in this pass. Do not publish a number until rechecked.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 10 personal online maps (team space: 3 collaborative maps); 3 sheets/map, 3-day history, 5 Pitch slides and 10 AI credits
tiers.notes: Desktop/mobile basic maps are available; the numeric caps above are for online/collaborative use.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Up to 50 manually created online maps; 3 sheets/map, 3-day history, unlimited Pitch slides and 10 AI credits
tiers.notes: Displayed yearly-billing equivalent; exact month-to-month price was not exposed in accessible official content.

tiers.name: Premium
tiers.limits: Unlimited collaborative maps and sheets; 30-day history; 500 AI credits/month; real-time collaboration, tasks and editable Gantt
tiers.notes: Displayed yearly-billing equivalent; exact month-to-month price was not exposed in accessible official content.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Unlimited collaborative maps/sheets; 30-day history; 800 AI credits/seat/month; team administration and editable Gantt
tiers.notes: Official Team page displays $10/seat/month and separately confirms a 7-day trial for the yearly plan; recorded as the displayed annual-plan equivalent.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Unlimited maps/sheets/history; custom AI credits; SAML SSO, onboarding and dedicated success support

pricing.freeTierCaps: Personal: 10 online maps, 3 sheets/map, 3-day history, 5 Pitch slides and 10 AI credits; Team space: 3 collaborative maps
pricing.billingTerms: monthly and annual for individual plans (up to 50% annual discount); Business yearly plan confirmed, exact monthly rates not publicly exposed
pricing.hiddenCosts: AI-generated maps can temporarily bypass Free/Pro manual-map limits while credits remain; credits expire/reset. One subscription covers up to 5 computers and 5 mobile devices. Monthly plans and AI-credit add-ons are non-refundable; yearly website purchases have a 7-day refund window. Xmind does not support downgrading an active higher tier.

verdictSummary: Xmind's solo core is compact: build a browser-based mind mapping editor with drag, resize, connect, keyboard shortcuts, autosave, and SVG or PNG export. A competent builder can reach a useful personal version in one sitting, while the paid product mainly wins on interaction polish, collaboration.
coreLoopDIY: Build a browser-based mind mapping editor with drag, resize, connect, keyboard shortcuts, autosave, and SVG or PNG export.
replacementScope: personal replacement for the core loop
whyPeopleStillPay: Xmind: The shapes are easy; customers pay for low-friction editing, reliable exports, collaboration, and a canvas that never fights them.
ongoingBurden: Own geometry, selection behavior, undo, clipboard interoperability, export fidelity, accessibility, and browser performance.

priorArt.name: Excalidraw
priorArt.desc: Open-source diagram canvas with an approachable interaction model.

alternatives.name: AFFiNE
alternatives.desc: Mind maps can turn into presentation frames and sit beside outlines, docs, and tasks; exports and visual refinement are not as mature as Xmind's.

facts.install: Hosted signup or desktop app; Docker Compose for self-hosting
facts.engines: Self-hosted AFFiNE AI can be configured with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, and FAL credentials
facts.dataFormat: Local-first clients keep workspace data locally and sync to AFFiNE Cloud or the operator's server; self-hosting uses PostgreSQL, Redis, and persistent blob storage
facts.gapVsPaid: AFFiNE's mind maps have fewer mature layouts, themes, exports, and polished presentation controls than Xmind's dedicated desktop and mobile product.
facts.setupBlocker: The hosted/desktop app installs cleanly; self-hosting is a multi-service Docker deployment that needs a domain, TLS, secrets, storage, backups, and AI-provider keys for AI features

alternatives.name: Freeplane
alternatives.desc: A serious desktop mind mapper with outlines, formulas, attributes, filters, and local files; excellent depth, unmistakably utilitarian furniture.

facts.install: Desktop installer/archive from the official download page; some Linux packages require a compatible Java runtime
facts.dataFormat: Mind maps are ordinary local .mm XML files and can export to formats including HTML, PDF, images, and office-document formats
facts.gapVsPaid: Freeplane is powerful but gives up Xmind's modern interface, mobile apps, real-time collaboration, visual polish, and smooth presentation mode.
facts.setupBlocker: The first obstacle is its traditional Java desktop packaging and interface; on Linux, users may also need to supply the right Java runtime or distribution package

alternatives.name: WiseMapping
alternatives.desc: Free hosted mind maps with collaboration and common import and export formats; no desktop application, offline workflow, or polished presentation mode.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or Docker deployment connected to PostgreSQL or MySQL
facts.dataFormat: Hosted maps live in WiseMapping's service; self-hosted maps and users live in the configured SQL database; maps import/export common mind-map and image/document formats
facts.gapVsPaid: WiseMapping has no comparable desktop or offline workflow and its visual refinement and presentation mode are substantially behind Xmind.
facts.setupBlocker: Hosted use is clean; self-hosting requires Docker and a database, and the custom public license requires a visible 'Powered by WiseMapping' notice throughout the user interface

notes: Strong page because Xmind separates a compact personal workflow from the value of long-term polish.
prompt:
Build a usable personal replacement for the core loop of Xmind.
Use exactly this stack: React + TypeScript + Vite + IndexedDB.
Primary job: Build a browser-based mind mapping editor with drag, resize, connect, keyboard shortcuts, autosave, and SVG or PNG export.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: multiplayer cursors and comments; large template libraries; high-fidelity import and export.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
